title: TODO scanner hardening makes clade-audit actionable
problem: After Cycle 13 made the hard gates truthful (Swift build, security, shell safety, error handling, dead code, retain cycles at zero), the TODO/FIXME inventory scanner was still emitting ~633 findings. The vast majority were false positives from substring keyword matching inside identifiers (Debug -> BUG, warning -> WARN, TODOItem -> TODO), matches inside markdown prose/tables, and scanning of planning docs, agent templates, and archived experiments.
solution: Rewrote the TODO scanner in rings/RUST-12/clade-audit/src/main.rs with three hardening slices: (1) should_skip_todo_path() excludes non-runtime docs/archives/agent/skill templates; (2) code_todo_match() requires comment markers and word boundaries for Swift/Rust files; (3) markdown_todo_match() only matches headings or task checkboxes. Also routed todo_check() through scannable_content() so the auditor's own source is skipped and Rust test modules are truncated.
result: TODO inventory dropped from ~633 to exactly 1 real finding (ChatViewModel.swift:474). Build, cargo test, cargo clippy, clade-e2e, and trios.app health all pass.
learnings: Substring keyword regexes on source code are almost always false-positive factories. Always anchor to comment markers and require word boundaries.
Markdown TODO checks must distinguish prose from explicit task items (- [ ] TODO:) and headings. Tables and inline lists otherwise drown the signal.
Reusing the existing scannable_content() helper kept the auditor from flagging its own test fixtures and test modules — a single point of reuse fixed an entire category of noise.
The noisiest gate often dominates the user experience of a self-critic dashboard. Cleaning it up is high leverage because it restores trust in the whole audit output.
mistakes: First iteration still left matches in clade-audit's own source because todo_check() was not using scannable_content(). Always run the audit after changing the auditor and inspect self-matches.

Initial markdown matcher was too permissive and kept a handful of false positives in trios-mesh/smoke/*.md and INSTALL_TODO.md. Path exclusions fixed the tail, but a stricter content-type matcher would have removed them naturally.
